summary: Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima (1898–1959) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Śrī Siṃha Shedra and under Tubten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, later teaching Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok, Tarthang Tulku, and others.

Boyd Michailovsky is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1976–1978) and at Langues et Civilisations à Tradition Orale (attested 1990).
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Byrski. She serves on the faculty at the University of Warsaw (attested 2026).

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned degrees from the University of Virginia (B.A. 1989, PhD 2004) and Harvard University (M.T.S. 1993), studying under David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Jeffrey Hopkins, and others.
Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. He served as Assistant Director at Boston University and held a post at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist. After studying at the University of Allahabad and under Mortimer Wheeler, he served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the IIAS (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson (born 1978) works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at Oxford under Charles Ramble and a habilitation at the University of Munich, holding posts at SOAS (~2005–2009) and the University of Munich (~2010–2018).
Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under the supervision of Patrick Pranke.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee (1932–2013) was an Indologist and historian. He earned a master's at the University of Calcutta and a doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later serving as Carmichael Professor at Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan S. Gillon works in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1980–1985) and has held posts in linguistics at McGill University, including Associate Professor (~1992) and faculty member (attested 2024–2025).

Bret W. Davis specializes in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, held research posts at Kyoto and Otani, and served as a philosophy professor at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).
Brian Bocking (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 1984), where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and under Geshe Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert (born 1962) specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Willis Stoesz. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018).

Brian Daizen Victoria (born 1939) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned degrees from Komazawa University and Temple University and held posts at the University of Auckland, Antioch University, Adelaide, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara (2005) and teaches Mongolian at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at East India Company College and Haileybury, and served as Assistant Resident and later British Resident at the Court of Nepal (~1820–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under Anne Carolyn Klein and also studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies.

Bridget Allchin (1927–2017) was an archaeologist and Indologist. She earned a PhD from University College London under Frederick Zeuner, became a Fellow of Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1978), and co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

Brigitte Marschall (born 1957) earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna, where she later served as an associate professor (außerordentliche Universitätsprofessorin, ~2000) and taught Mungunchimeg Batmunkh.
